channel.title: NPR Topics: Education
channel.description: We've been to school. We know how education works. Right? In fact, many aspects of learning — in homes, at schools, at work and elsewhere — are evolving rapidly, along with our understanding of learning. Join us as we explore how learning happens.

item.title: How community colleges are evolving to fill local data center jobs
item.description: Community colleges are often charged with training students for the jobs that already exist in their communities. But what if the jobs that need filling are at a data center?

item.title: The federal law aimed at protecting college students from sexual abuse

item.title: Schools are experimenting with AI with little evidence or policy to guide them
item.description: Teachers are using AI to develop lesson plans, and in some districts, AI chatbots give students feedback on their work. Meanwhile, the research around how AI can help students is extremely limited.

item.title: The Education Dept. hasn't been dismantled. It's become more inefficient, staff say
item.description: Education staff are being scattered across several other federal agencies. Despite the Trump administration's claims, employees say it's adding bureaucracy and making it harder to serve students.
